national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of households in Bosnia and Herzegovina covered by a fixed very high capacity network (VHCN). It includes households with access to fibre-to-the-premises networks (FTTP), including FTTH and FTTB, as well as cable networks using DOCSIS 3.1 technology or higher. Coverage is expressed as a percentage of the total number of households.
national_rationale: Data on household coverage by fixed very high capacity networks in Bosnia and Herzegovina were provided by the Communications Regulatory Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina (RAK), based on data submitted to the Agency by electronic communications operators. The data refer to 2025 and cover the number of households with access to FTTP networks (FTTH and FTTB) and cable networks using DOCSIS 3.1 technology or higher. According to RAK data, a total of 418,323 households in Bosnia and Herzegovina are covered by at least one of these technologies, taking into account overlaps in coverage between different networks and operators. Of these, 408,383 households are covered by FTTP networks, while 9,940 households are covered by cable networks using DOCSIS 3.1 technology or higher. An indicative estimate provided by the Demography Sector of the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BHAS) was used for the total number of households.
national_methodology_characteristics: For Bosnia and Herzegovina, data are available for 2025, when RAK calculated the indicator for the first time based on data submitted by electronic communications operators. RAK also reported that operators in Bosnia and Herzegovina predominantly provide services through DOCSIS 3.0 cable networks, while only three operators provided services through DOCSIS 3.1 or higher networks during the reference period. Therefore, the indicator includes only households with access to technologies that meet the VHCN definition, and not all households covered by cable networks. When interpreting the 2025 value, it should be taken into account that the total number of households used in the calculation is based on an indicative estimate that does not represent a reliable figure for 2025. Comparable data are not available for previous years, which means that it is not possible to analyse the time trend or calculate progress compared with the previous period.
national_long_objective: The development and availability of very high capacity networks are important prerequisites for improving digital connectivity, developing electronic communications and expanding the use of digital services in Bosnia and Herzegovina. No specific quantitative national target has been established for this indicator in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The European Union's 2030 target, according to which all European households should be covered by a gigabit network, represents an EU strategic objective and should not be interpreted as an official national target for Bosnia and Herzegovina.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of households covered by a fixed very high capacity network (VHCN), including FTTP and qualifying DOCSIS 3.1 cable networks. Data can be broken down by type of area.
eu_rationale: The data are based on the Broadband Coverage in Europe study, conducted for the European Commission, namely the Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology (DG CNECT). Data are collected from electronic communications operators and refer to the availability of network infrastructure to households. Coverage is expressed as a percentage of the total number of households.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers households with access to a fixed very high capacity network, namely an FTTP network or a cable network using DOCSIS 3.1 technology or higher. Data are collected annually and allow monitoring of coverage developments and comparisons between EU Member States, as well as between urban and rural areas.
eu_long_objective: Under the EU Digital Decade targets for 2030, all households in the EU should be covered by a gigabit network, and all populated areas should have access to 5G networks.
